name: Ras al Jinz Turtle Reserve and Arabian Sea coast
blurb: Green turtles nest on warm sand beside one of the richest seas on Earth.

tip.title: Remove the green turtles
tip.text: Set Green turtle to -100% and watch the ghost crabs, red foxes and gulls lose eggs and hatchlings, the tiger shark lose its main prey, and seagrass and algae go ungrazed.

sources.title: UNESCO tentative list: Ras al Hadd Turtle Reserve and Ras al Jinz

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Strong year-round sun drives algae and seagrass growth in the clear shallows and warms the sand where turtle eggs incubate.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Microbes and scavenging invertebrates break down dead animals, eggs and plant matter, returning nutrients to sand and lagoon.
Drifting microscopic algae that bloom when monsoon upwelling brings nutrients up; the base of the open-water food chain.
Seagrass meadows in warm shallow water are the main food of adult green turtles, and shelter young fish.

nodes.name: Sea lettuce
nodes.desc: A green seaweed of rocky and shallow shores that green turtles are recorded grazing.
Salt-tolerant tree that grows in scattered stands in the lagoons, where it stabilises mud and shelters young fish and crabs.

nodes.name: Copepods
nodes.desc: Tiny crustaceans that graze phytoplankton and are in turn eaten by small fish.

nodes.name: Green turtle
nodes.desc: Adults graze seagrass and algae; females nest on the beaches of Ras al Jinz and Ras al Hadd year-round. The reserve is among the world's most important green turtle nesting sites.
Burrowing beach crabs that hunt and scavenge at night; crabs are among the predators of turtle hatchlings crossing the sand.
A wader with a heavy bill specialised for eating crabs; it nests in burrows in sandy banks around the Arabian Sea.
A fish-eating raptor that hunts by diving; commonly recorded along this coast.
An opportunistic predator and scavenger; red foxes are known to dig up and eat sea turtle eggs.
A large shark and the main natural predator of sea turtles of all sizes.
A shallow coastal dolphin that feeds on fish, squid and crustaceans, with important populations along the Arabian Peninsula.
